clue.text: Bang on about revolutionary cleric

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns round, so the short word for about is turned back to front

parts.note: CA is circa, the Latin abbreviation for about
a curate is an assistant clergyman

explanation.surface: Someone is spot on in describing a radical churchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' looks like it describes the cleric, but it turns CA (about) into AC.
explanation.definitionFit: Bang on is an idiom for exactly right, precise and correct.

clue.text: Entrée of fancy cheeses on a regular basis

indicators.note: on a regular basis says take every other letter of the words fancy cheeses, starting from the second

explanation.surface: A posh starter is made of a selection of fine cheeses.
explanation.walkthrough: Entrée is not the course here but its other sense, admission.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrée is a right of admission or entry into a place or circle.

clue.text: Defends a politician wearing tight chinos

indicators.note: wearing means the trousers go round, enclosing the other pieces
tight is slang for drunk, so the letters of chinos are jumbled

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An MP has squeezed into a pair of snug trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight' reads as snug-fitting trousers, but it is slang for drunk and turns the trousers into CHIONS.
explanation.definitionFit: To champion a cause is to speak up for and support it, a synonym of defend.

clue.text: Concerned with a relation's explanations

parts.note: re means concerning or with regard to
a son is a relation; with the apostrophe-s it gives the word plus S

explanation.surface: Someone is worried about a family member's excuses.
explanation.definitionFit: Reasons are the grounds or justifications offered to explain something.

clue.text: Name bird by pasture with no tail

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

indicators.note: with no tail means the last letter of the meadow word is cut off

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or pasture

explanation.surface: Someone names a tailless bird found beside a field.
explanation.definitionFit: A title is the name of a book, film or piece of work.

clue.text: Got hold of hot stuff and used foil?

definitions.meaning: to fence goods is to handle stolen property, which is hot
a foil is a light fencing sword, so using one means taking part in that sport

explanation.surface: A cook grabbed something hot and wrapped it in kitchen foil.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses hide behind the kitchen: hot stuff is stolen goods, and foil is the slim sword, not the wrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: A receiver of stolen goods is a fence; sabre, épée and foil duellists practise fencing.

clue.text: Each short afternoon nap could be most amenable

indicators.note: short says the nap word loses its final letter

parts.note: a siesta is a nap after lunch

explanation.surface: Taking a brief nap after lunch every day might make anyone most agreeable.
explanation.definitionFit: Easiest describes whatever gives least trouble, the most tractable or compliant.

clue.text: Tweet from Republican enthralled by golf shot

indicators.note: enthralled by means held inside, so the shot word surrounds the letter

parts.note: a chip is a short lofted golf shot

explanation.surface: A Republican posts online, captivated by a golf stroke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tweet' suggests a social media post, but it is a bird's call.
explanation.definitionFit: A chirp and a tweet are both the short high call of a small bird.

clue.text: Is tense in formal clothing, producing suffering

indicators.note: in means these letters are placed inside the clothing word

parts.note: dress as in evening dress or formal dress
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A person is uptight in their smart clothes, which causes them misery.
explanation.definitionFit: Distress is mental or physical pain, anguish or hardship.

clue.text: View for spectators half concealed

parts.note: pro means for or in favour of, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: half concealed says the back half of the word spectators is hidden, leaving its first half

explanation.surface: The sight-lines for the audience are partly blocked.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospect is an extensive view or vista of a landscape.

clue.text: Scratchier cat is unfortunately making marks

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cat that scratches more is, sadly, leaving marks on the furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Distinguishing marks are the features or traits that identify something.

clue.text: What if model is after drink?

indicators.note: after means the posing word comes second, following the drinking word

parts.note: to sup is to drink
to model is to pose

explanation.surface: A speculative question: what if a model has had a drink?
explanation.definitionFit: Both introduce a hypothetical, as in 'imagine that' or 'let us assume'.

clue.text: Returning fish for a kipper?

indicators.note: returning means the fish word is read backwards

parts.note: eels are long thin fish
per means for each or for a, as in miles per hour

explanation.surface: Swapping one fish for a smoked herring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kipper' looks like the smoked fish, matching the surface, but it is someone who kips, British slang for sleeps.
explanation.definitionFit: One who kips, or takes a nap, is someone asleep, playfully named after the slang verb.

clue.text: Very impertinent language after unknown addition to a meal

indicators.note: after puts the cheeky talk behind the unknown

parts.note: so means very, as in so good
Y is a mathematical unknown
sauce is cheeky talk

explanation.surface: Someone was very rude after an unexpected guest joined dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A salty condiment made from fermented beans is a common extra at the table.

clue.text: Do end flu upset that's developed

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A plea to beat the flu that has taken hold.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan or story that unfolded has opened out, evolved or developed.

clue.text: Male in chains for ages

indicators.note: in means the letter goes inside the chains word

parts.note: ties are bonds or chains

explanation.surface: A man held in chains for a long while.
explanation.definitionFit: Times and ages both mean eras or long periods, as in olden times.

clue.text: Engineer getting work on island? On the contrary

indicators.note: on the contrary reverses the stated order, so island goes on top of work instead of work on island

parts.note: the Isle of Man is an island in the Irish Sea
oeuvre is French for a work, used for an artist's body of work

explanation.surface: An engineer is posted to work on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: To engineer a result is to contrive or arrange it cleverly, a skilful move.

clue.text: University about to infiltrate sects' lifestyles

indicators.note: to infiltrate means to get inside, so these letters go within the sects word

parts.note: cults are sects
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A university is about to plant spies in religious groups to study how they live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' reads as 'on the point of', but 'about' is RE and 'to infiltrate' the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Cultures are the customs and ways of life of a group of people.

clue.text: Out of bed and ready to be annoyed

parts.note: up means risen from bed
set means ready, as in ready, steady, go

explanation.surface: Someone has just woken and is ready to get cross.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone upset is distressed or put out, a near synonym of annoyed.

clue.text: Notices bloodsucking mites eating alien

indicators.note: eating means the mites word swallows the other letters

parts.note: ticks are bloodsucking arachnids related to mites
ET is the film alien, the extra-terrestrial

explanation.surface: Warning signs about parasites devouring an extraterrestrial.
explanation.definitionFit: A parking or speeding ticket is an official notice of a penalty.

clue.text: Getting charming

definitions.meaning: going to collect and bring back something

explanation.surface: Becoming delightful.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is going and bringing something back; the other means attractive, as in a fetching hat.

clue.text: Animal meat knight cut from tail

parts.note: ham is cured pork

indicators.note: cut from means the knight's letter is removed from the tail word

parts.note: the stern is the rear or tail end, as of a ship
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A butcher trims a knight's portion of meat from the tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A small burrowing rodent with cheek pouches, often kept as a pet.

clue.text: What teacher provides without working?

parts.note: less means minus or without
on means operating or working, as of a switched-on machine

explanation.surface: What does a teacher deliver when not in employment?
explanation.definitionFit: A class or period of instruction is what a schoolteacher gives.

clue.text: Play it cool at first, changing routine

indicators.note: changing means these letters are altered into a new order
at first says take only the opening letter of cool

explanation.surface: Advice to stay calm at first while varying a set performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Typical and routine both mean normal, ordinary, run of the mill.

clue.text: Student's flipping cheek at university

indicators.note: flipping means turning over, so the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: lip is cheeky talk
up means in residence at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: A student is being insolent at college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' reads as a mild British swear word but signals the turnaround; 's is the link 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil is a learner at school or under a tutor.

clue.text: Partly insincere, PM occasionally repelled host

indicators.note: repelled means driven back, so the run of letters is read backwards
partly means only a portion of the following words is used, a run of their letters

explanation.surface: A rather insincere Prime Minister sometimes turned away a host.
explanation.definitionFit: A compere is the master of ceremonies who hosts a show.

clue.text: Understand cleric at church? To an extent

indicators.note: To an extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Can you follow a vicar's sermon in church? Only partly.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch a remark is to hear and grasp it, as in 'I didn't catch that'.

clue.text: Reforms save enterprise — about time, MPs!

indicators.note: about means going round, so the jumbled letters surround the time letter
reforms means remakes, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A demand that MPs finally pass reforms rescuing business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about time' reads as an exasperated 'at last', but 'about' is the insertion and 'time' is T.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of Parliament sit in the House of Commons as elected delegates of voters.

clue.text: Drop news story

definitions.meaning: a small quantity of liquid, such as a dash of soda
a prominent front-page item in a paper

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a dash of liquid; the other a sensational headline item in a newspaper.

clue.text: One enters her tent drunk — this could be unlucky

indicators.note: enters means goes inside, so the numeral is placed within the jumbled letters
drunk suggests staggering, so the letters of her tent are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone drunk barges into a woman's tent, which could bring bad luck.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirteen is the number superstition holds to be unlucky.
